reviews.comment: You can tell Professor Okoromadu is a nice guy, but he is a really horrible professor. He encourages discussion in his class but then immediately shoots down points of view he doesn't agree with. Extremely difficult to stay awake during his boring Friday morning lectures.
Professor Tony was such an efficient teacher that the finance department decided to remove him (obviously to work on more important things).
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This Prof literally got replaced halfway through the 5-week course. Tony seems like a super nice guy, but expects you to do everything on your own outside of class. He refuses to work example problems at any time either in class or office hours/email. Almost everyone failed the first exam. Hoping for a better rest of the class with the new prof.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exam 1 had an average of 50% but I pulled a 65. Lectured straight out of the textbook and didn't do a single practice problem. Three days before Exam 1 he sends out 'Self Check Quizzes' and no one can solve a single problem. Spent the next two days teaching myself the class. Told us to drop the class post-exam after we voiced our complaints.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE. The professor is so inconsiderate of his students. The first exam had an average of about a 50%. Expects us to take exam 2 in 5 class days, when it took him 2.5 weeks to teach us the material for exam 1. Does not prepare you for exams He expects you to learn all math by yourself. I am mainly A, w/ few B student, this class was horrible

Attendance is nearly half of the final grade and DONT be like me and assume he is bluffing about taking it each class. Didn't put in a single grade til AFTER semester ended and was SO rude and demeaning in emails to the class when students would ask about grades. Some kids literally had no idea if they were passing in order to graduate. Crazy

I cannot stress this enough, he sucks at teaching. He will read to you in class then ask questions that are unrelated to the reading. All exam questions require you to read his mind to choose what he thinks is the BEST answer (even if you can prove he is wrong). Spends lots time talking down to students and will mock you in office hours

Material is straight forward and pretty easy, but his test questions are poorly written and confusingly worded. Incredibly condescending both in class and in office hours. Most frustrating professor I've ever had. He refuses to schedule exams at the start of the semester, so all of our exams were crammed into the last month of the semester.
Dont take him for 341 if youre a finance major. He read through the textbook in the lectures, so it was very monotonous.

If you're not a finance major, take this prof during the summer. He's not good at teaching but there are other ways to finesse you're way through the class without tutor john. It's only a month of your life, power through. I managed to get a B+ and I did not know what was going on, so you got this. Collaborate w/ classmates for project it will help

I may have said lecture heavy, but his lectures are just reading the textbook. Exams are heavily based on math, not to mention exams (and the 40% leveled project) are poorly spaced out. Having half of your grade in a span of 3 days is strenuous. I would recommend TutorJohn, Chris does a good job of explaining problems that will be on the exams.

This prof is genuinely nice as most comments say. However, I would avoid him for finance 341. He does not announce test dates ahead of time. Had the summer class take exam 1 and 2 within 2 days of each other due to a university cancellation. Final project was very last minute but expect a lot of work and he grades it hard. Tutor John is a necessity

DO NOT TAKE Worst structured course I've ever taken, worst curriculum Mays has to offer. He only reads the textbook and does no workout problems whatsoever geared towards the test. First test was 3-1/2 weeks into a 5-week course, and two days before test #2. Got the most time-consuming project worth 40% three days before it was due. MUST GO TO TJ.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: No schedule of exams or anything. His lecture's are not that helpful despite him stressing understanding concepts is good to pass exams. Just depend on learning through your peers and TAs/help desk. He means well and wants to help but it's just difficult especially a 5week course with minimal planning and dropping a project on you last minutes
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: After half of the class failed the first exam, he went back and found a faulty question, then proceeded to TAKE AWAY points from people after already publishing their grades. I've never heard of a prof doing that before.

He is a nice guy but a bad professor. His lectures are not that helpful because all he does is read from the textbook (he does provide pdfs of the chapters used) and does not give any examples of problems. He also does not curve tests despite the fact on our first test about half of the people failed despite it being open note/book. dont recommend

I don't recommend this class. All he does in lectures is read the textbook, he doesn't explain any of the important stuff. You basically have to teach yourself the material. Also, very poor planner. I took this class over the summer and the first test got cancelled last minute so he moved it to 2 days before our next test. Don't take!
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Okoromadu is a genuinely nice guy. This class is meant to be a discussion class, but participation basically becomes bonus points. There are few assignments that don't take much work. Instructions can be a bit ambiguous, but if you ask for clarification he's glad to help you out. Easy class. Lectures can be dull, but he's a great guy.

The class is so ambiguous. He always wants students to speak up, but if you don't answer with a response or make a point he thinks is good enough, he will talk down to you. Tough to please and his tests are not the easiest.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: most people made the mistake of taking him in the summer. Thinking its easier, DO NOT DO THIS! His gpa is only higher because it includes people who ended up dropping and already have an idea of the material of this course. Take guyton in the fall/spring.

Professor Okoromadu taught FINC341 over the summer and I thought he did pretty good for his first time for this class. The first test was Tough but the last two test were super easy. The final project was definitely tough and took a lot of work. IF you actually listen and participate in his lectures you will understand the material.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The usual professor for this class is Guyton, but over the summer of 2020, it was Okoromadu. To sum up my experience with him I would say he is a nice guy and that's it. Everything you need to know in this course you have to learn on your own. The only reason I would take him again as his lectures are easier to sit through than Guyton's.
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Tony was a GREAT prof! I know theres negative reviews but I felt as though he really wants you to understand the material not just memorize. He was so patient and went over concepts and formulas over and over until you got it. He really cares about his students! The only negative in my opinion was he didnt give test dates up front.

Nice guy, but does not teach very effectively. I took a 5 week summer course and he barely got through any of the information needed for each test. His lectures were absolutely not helpful for any of the test. Gave a mini project a week before it was due that was worth 40% of our grade and had unreasonable expectations. DO NOT TAKE!!

No test dates were given upfront, and it took the prof 3 weeks to teach material for test 1 (this was a 5-week class!) We didn't even get to finish the material, which is frustrating as I am a FINC major. Tony is a super sweet guy, but has obviously never taught FINC 341 and was not prepared. Don't even get me started on the mini-project.

This professor seemed nice enough but was by no means a good professor. He only read word for word from the book and only taught a finance problem once. Additionally, the mini project counts for 40% of your grade and he does not teach how to do it and gets mad when outside sources such as tutoring is used. Would not recommend taking this professor.

Lectures are powerpoints consisting of screenshots of a textbook. He then lets a computerized voice read the words off the screenshots of the textbook. He is the epitome of lazy, unorganized, and unqualified to teach. He asks for students opinions on ethical issues and then dismisses any opinions he does not agree with as incorred and of no value
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: It is frustrating to have no exam dates given up front, but Tony really does care about his students. He WANTS you to go into his office hours and talk to him about what you think about the course and the readings. If you have 0 patience, do not take. If you are okay with ambiguity, and want to work for participation points, take him for an A!
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Participation matters
